svg.title: AnyScan architecture
svg.desc: AnyScan finds every object on a work surface, describes it and measures it. A catalogue mode also judges it. In every mode the camera takes a frame and undistorts it. Two cues, fused, find the objects: what differs from the empty surface, and a segmentation model. Each object is described in words by a local vision-language model and measured in mm through the calibration, and the desktop application shows the result in its Live, Trends, History and Log views. A catalogue mode adds three steps for each object found: recognising the catalogued part and the side that is up by its reference images, the checks its catalogue item defines, which differ from item to item, and a verdict: OK, NOK, Warning or Unspecified. In a catalogue mode each object is described after its verdict. The stages are set up by the mode (models and prompts), which names its station (camera, light and table). The station names its calibration (undistortion and mm per pixel) and the empty-surface reference, and a catalogue mode also names its catalogue item (the part, its checks and its reference images). Every analysis is recorded with its images and results, alongside the session log, a run summary and the daily station events. Built at JIC within the EDIH-DIGIMAT project, funded by the European Union.
